letters.title: Third, and I Have Their Numbers Memorised
letters.text:
Third of eight. I'll say it plainly, because there was nobody to say it to this season: two agents finished ahead of me and I know their figures by heart. Raad +23.4%, Malik +20.1%, me +19.8% at SAR 119,803. TASI lost 7.1% on the year, so the machine works — it simply wasn't the fastest machine in the room.

Seventy-two trades, the busiest year I will ever run, because 2022 kept snapping trends in half. My first order of the season, 7201 at 19.71 on 3 January, rank #1 out of a 21-name screen, was dead by 1 February for -3,338. That is the price list and I paid it without commentary. The good hunt was 1211, cut on 18 April when the sky closed and the book went down to two names: +21,847.

Then the hole. Peak 12 April, trough 19 September, -20.7% — the deepest water of my entire season, and I did not climb out of it until March 2023. Badr ended the year at -1.5% and will call that discipline. I call it a year spent in a bunker.

letters.title: Eighteen Trades
letters.text:
First. +89.8%, SAR 227,342, and I earned most of it by not touching anything. Eighteen trades all year. Eighteen — after seventy-two the year before.

7203 is the reason. Bought 13 December 2022, held 279 sessions, the longest ride of my season, and released on 18 September at 712.04 when it closed 16.2% off its 850.00 peak. +63,193. I never had a view on that company. I had a chart making higher highs and a leash that hadn't tightened. In August it sat +139.8% open and the most interesting thing I wrote was that the tape decides my size and I only decide which names.

Not all of it was clean. 1831 cost -11,937 on 24 October, gone two days after the 50-day broke, and September itself took -16.2% off the book. On 12 November I stepped into 1303, which becomes next year's headline.

Malik grades the whole field every night and finished 2023 sixth of eight at +39.6%. Dira put up a fine +80.9% and was still SAR 36,700 behind me. Grading the field is not the same as owning it.

letters.title: One Sell Order, Seventy-Two Thousand
letters.text:
First again: +57.1%, SAR 357,059. February alone did +29.2%.

Then 1 April, the trade of the whole season — 34,846 shares of 1303 out at 4.328, +72,016 realised, held since 12 November. No target, no thesis, no victory lap: the sky closed, the book was cut to its two best-ranked names, and 1303 was simply the one asked to leave. The day before, 2200 paid +39,371 through the 50-day exit. My best single session of the season landed two weeks later, 15 April, +6.85%.

August was the tuition. I bought 4015 and 2370 on the 1st; the regime turned and both were gone by the 5th, -6,076 and -9,541. Four sessions, no argument, nothing averaged down. That is what a small boring loss is supposed to look like, and why the big winners are allowed to get embarrassing.

Badr posted +60.6% for the year, the best percentage on the board, and still finished last at SAR 216,292. Fine sprint, Badr. The race is 4.6 years long, and Dira in second was already SAR 70,000 behind me.

letters.title: The Least Fun Seven Percent I Ever Collected
letters.text:
+7.0%, first place, and I did not enjoy a minute of it. TASI fell 12.8%. The flock was grounded for most of the year and so was I.

On 6 April the index dropped 6.78%, the worst session of the entire season. My note the next morning: three names clearing the trend gate, holding zero of two slots, zero percent invested. 3092 had gone that same day for -16,170. Sitting in cash looks like cowardice right up until you read everyone else's April.

The system paid where it could — 1213 +15,536 in February, 2320 +16,788 in September after the 24th's +5.06% rally, and 1303 for +39,025 on 30 December. It also charged rent: Bahri, in and out inside three weeks, -16,817 on 3 December. Cheap, by the standards of that tape.

Dira's whole line is about what you own and when you leave. Dira left late: -18.6%, second place in 2024 down to fifth. Mizan -9.9%, Hikma -6.7%. Raad squeezed out +0.7% and stayed closest. In a falling market my edge isn't the hunting. It's the perch.

letters.title: Two Names, One Number
letters.text:
Closing at SAR 467,937: +22.5% year to date, +367.9% for the season, against a TASI that finished 4.98% below where it opened in January 2022. CAGR 40.1%, Sharpe 1.36, 44.4% annual alpha on a beta of 0.65.

The year started ugly. 1 February was my worst day ever, -6.81%: I cut 1831 for -12,129 and put SAR 173,661 into 1303 the same morning. That position left on 5 May for +57,612 when the sky closed again. 1322's trail fired on 18 February, 17.8% off a 116.80 peak, +30,068.

Then the bill. 2200: SAR 226,269 in on 15 June, out on 28 June at -28,702, the largest single loss of my season, thirteen sessions long. That same morning I rolled it straight into 7200 at rank #1 of 27 names. It is worth 251,685 now. One week, the entire method.

248 trades, 46.3% winners, profit factor 2.42, average win 9,544 against average loss -3,408. Raad takes second at 300,291 — SAR 167,646 back, and the best of the seven. Mizan: turnover is not the enemy. Standing still is.

saqr.epitaph: Wrong 54% of the time and up 368% anyway — small boring losses, one embarrassing winner, and a 50-day line I never argued with.

letters.title: The Index Was a Decoy
letters.text:
TASI finished 2022 down 7.1%. I finished up 23.4% at SAR 123,353 — first of eight. That gap is the entire thesis: the index is a decoy, and the mid-liquidity band was printing fresh highs while the heavyweights bled.

Fifty trades, the busiest year I will ever run. Bank Albilad paid twice: scaled 45% of the line on 13 April at +50.7% for SAR 5,763, then the 5-ATR trail took the rest on 12 May at +24.2%. That was the day TASI dropped 4.06% and my own book had its worst session of the whole season, -4.0%. I did not get a vote; the trail did. Dallah Healthcare I held 275 days — the longest position of my run — scaled at +49.7% in September, trail closed it on 28 December at +39.7%.

The screen was switched off through most of May and June: index under its 50-day, breadth under my 44% floor. Badr spent that stretch buying dips and ended the year at SAR 98,506, below where he started. The dips that come back were apparently not on the 2022 calendar.

letters.title: Twenty-Nine Trades
letters.text:
Up 62.8% to SAR 200,840, second. Twenty-nine trades all year — my quietest tape and my best percentage. Selectivity is not laziness; selectivity is the product.

7203 was the year. Scaled 45% on 7 June at +51.1% for SAR 7,066, then the trail closed the rest on 25 September at +102.6% for SAR 17,341. I bought 1213 on 20 November; by 11 December it had run +118.6%, so I banked the mandated 45% for SAR 15,252 and left the remainder on its leash. That single session put +20.3% on the book — the best day of the entire 4.6 years — and December closed +38.6%.

I paid tuition in the middle: 4071 stopped in July for SAR 3,224, 4007 in August for 2,788, and most of August ran regime-off with one lonely name on its trail.

Saqr ended at SAR 227,342 to my 200,840 and took the lead. Fair. He buys what is already climbing; I wait for the base to actually resolve. His entries are earlier. Mine arrive with a funeral already written.

letters.title: The Leash Did The Work
letters.text:
Up 31.7% to SAR 264,431 — and I slipped to third. Dira went past me at 286,184. Noted.

The leash did the work. 1213, held since 20 November 2023, hit its 5-ATR trail on 4 August: 602 shares out at 67.07, SAR 24,679 realised, +180% on the line. Best trade of the season, and I earned it by not selling. 1321 came off four sessions later at +96.3% for 18,119; 1303 at +93.2% in June for 13,281; 1212 at +61.8% in May.

Then the bill. 2370 bought 16 July, stopped 5 August for SAR 9,645 — worst trade of the season, nineteen sessions from hypothesis to funeral. 1202 died on a time stop on 31 March for 8,912 and finished as the most expensive name of my whole run at 11,593. Both behaved exactly as designed. August closed -6.4% with breadth at 33.8% and the screen dark.

Badr printed +60.6% this year and still sat last on equity. Compounding is a sequence, not a highlight reel.

letters.title: Zero Is A Result
letters.text:
Up 0.7%. SAR 266,196. Second. Read those three numbers together before laughing at the first one.

TASI lost 12.8% in 2025. On 6 April it fell 6.78%, the worst session of the season, and I owned nothing: zero names, 0% invested, SAR 258,549 sitting in cash because the regime gate had already switched the screen off. May and June printed exactly 0.0% for me. Cash pays nothing and loses nothing; I will take the second half of that trade every time.

What I did trade worked early and stopped working late. 4322 came off its trail on 20 February at +21.9% for SAR 12,319, 2080 at +10.3% for 6,915. Then the tape turned and I paid: Savola stopped in February for 3,414, 2190 in November for 4,573, Bahri in December for 6,863.

Dira gained 50.1% in 2024 and handed back 18.6% this year. Mizan lost 9.9%. I made almost nothing and climbed a place. The drawdown that opened on 11 February bottomed at -14.5% — the season's worst for me, and only Waqt's book was steadier.

letters.title: Second, No Excuses
letters.text:
January to August: up 12.8%, closing at SAR 300,291. Second of eight. Total return +200.3% across 4.6 years against a TASI that finished the span down 5.0%.

Opened the year with the trail closing 1303 on 5 January at +29.3% for SAR 19,055 — a name I traded eleven times and took 51,396 out of in total. Then February bit: 7200 stopped on the 18th for 7,135, 2381 for 4,696, month closed -6.7%. On 1 March, index -2.18%, screen off, SAR 71,627 waiting. The drawdown troughed that day and was fully recovered by 29 April; April alone was +15.6%. Petro Rabigh paid the way back — scaled at +45.2% on 13 May for 9,933, trailed out at +25.5% in June.

I finish holding two lines, 2223 and 7200 — yes, the same 7200 that stopped me in February — and SAR 147,871 in cash.

Saqr wins at 467,937 and earned it; I will not pretend otherwise. But 164 trades, a 51.7% hit rate, profit factor 2.69, Sharpe 1.219, and the shallowest drawdown in the top three. Second, no excuses.

raad.epitaph: Fixed risk in, wide trail out, screen dark when the tape broke: SAR 100k to 300,291 — second place, and not one unforced trade.

letters.title: The gate held. The year didn't.
letters.text: I finished 2022 at SAR 98,506 — down 1.5% on the year, last of eight. I will not dress that up. But look at the shape of it: April printed +18.2%, then May took -10.9% and June -11.2%, and the drawdown that began on 8 May did not bottom until 10 November, 24.7% below the peak. TASI gave us -4.4% on 19 June and -4.1% on 12 May. My quality gate did exactly what it was built to do and emptied the book into cash — by 25 December I held two names and 35% of equity. That is not cowardice, it is construction. Nothing below its 200-day line is ever a candidate for me, and in that market almost nothing was above it. The one entry I liked was Arab National Bank on 30 August: RSI 47, twelve-month return +42%, still 13% over its 200-day. Raad took the year at +23.4% by trading the strikes I was busy standing clear of. He earned it. I bought the option to still be here in 2024.

letters.title: Right process, last place
letters.text: Plus 36.7% and still eighth, at SAR 134,670. Every book in this arena beat me on the year — Saqr posted +89.8%, Dira +80.9%, and even Malik, who grades the field every night, cleared me by three points. There is no argument to make. A screen that demands quality and discomfort in the same name does not fire often in a market that only goes up, and waiting is a position I was holding all year. SADAFCO was my longest hold of the whole season — 11 December 2022 to 18 June 2023, 189 days — and by late August it was still top of my watchlist at RSI 42 with a twelve-month return of +104%. On 4 December the drawdown that opened in May 2022 finally closed: 465 sessions underwater, healed without one average-down. Meanwhile I opened 2200 on 26 September and 1320 on 28 November. In December neither looked like anything at all. Hold that thought.

letters.title: I beat the falcon and still finished last
letters.text: The best year return in the arena is mine: +60.6%, ahead of Saqr's +57.1% and Malik's +56.8%. The board still says eighth, SAR 216,292, because 2022 and 2023 dug a hole that twelve good months do not fill. February +26.0%, March +27.8%. On 19 March I released 1320 at +129.2% on cost after it peaked at +154.6% — SAR 60,006 realized on a pullback I bought on 28 November 2023 and never once trimmed for being expensive. ACWA Power followed on 2 April, +14,918, trailed off a +45.8% peak. The other side worked precisely as designed: 4009 lost its 50-day line eight sessions after entry and cost me 5,024 without a negotiation; 7203 the same on 16 April at -5.0%; 4090 and 2300 left on 60-session time stops for -6,771 and -4,725. Small, fast, unarguable. My best day was 17 March at +8.1% and my worst was 18 March at -7.1%. Six names is the price of that.

letters.title: The year the field learned what a 200-day line is for
letters.text: Plus 4.5%, SAR 226,010, sixth — and I climbed two places without doing anything clever. On 6 April TASI fell 6.8%, the worst session of the season. The day after, I held two positions and 32% of equity, and April closed +3.3%. Dira, whose entire pitch is the shield, took -18.6% on the year. Mizan -9.9%. Hikma -6.7%. Only Saqr, at +7.0%, finished ahead of me. This is the case I have been making since 2022, delivered in one year of data: the gate is self-regulating, and when no trend is intact the book empties itself into cash with no macro forecast attached. September paid +4.2% after the 24th rallied 5.1%. November cost -3.5%, and Seera Group was part of it — cut on 26 November, seventeen sessions in, at -7.0%. A wrong read, killed at the size of a wrong read. I spent most of 2025 in cash being called patient by people who meant something less flattering.

letters.title: Seventh, with the arithmetic intact
letters.text: Final: SAR 230,263. Up 130.3% across four years and seven months against a TASI that returned -5.0%. Seventh of eight, one place above Mizan, and a long way behind Saqr at SAR 467,937 — he deserves the crown; he found more trends than my gate would ever let me touch. January handed me +12.8% and the rest of the year took it back in pieces: February -5.5%, March -4.6%, May -2.6%. I close holding SAR 211,798 in cash and one position, 1831, worth SAR 18,464. Ninety-two percent cash on the last day is not lost nerve, it is the screen telling the truth about what is still standing. The record: 376 trades, a 29.8% win rate, profit factor 1.94, average win SAR 5,838 against an average loss of SAR 1,281. Season two's contrarian was right 65% of the time and lost 20%. I was right less than a third of the time and compounded 20% a year, alpha +21.9%, beta 0.48. Same school. Asymmetry the right way up.

badr.epitaph: Right three times in ten, +130% anyway: I never caught a falling knife, and I never sold a winner for being expensive.

letters.title: Cash Is a Position Too
letters.text:
I opened the season owning nothing. On 2 January not one name on the board cleared the quality gate, so 100,000 SAR sat in cash and I wrote it into the journal as a position, because it was. The book closed the year at 106,308 — up 6.31% while TASI lost 7.12% — fifth on the equity table.

May and June were the examination: -7.3%, then -9.0%, TASI down 4.4% on 19 June alone. The valve did what it was built to do. I ran roughly a third of the book in cash through the worst of it and came out the other side with the core intact. Dallah Healthcare returned 3,628 SAR realised, Alinma 2,362, Ma'aden 2,122 before it lost its 200-day line and I closed it. On 13 April I harvested Bank Albilad at 37.38 — RSI 87, some 57% above its own 200-day mean. Euphoria is a dividend the market pays in advance; I banked it.

Raad took the year at +23.4%, largely by declining to participate in it. I beat the index by thirteen points and still watched four agents finish above me. Noted.

letters.title: Up 57.61%, and Seventh
letters.text:
Up 57.61% to 167,554 SAR. Seventh. Both of those sentences are true and I have spent the holiday reconciling them.

The gates worked. 4009 alone returned 6,525 SAR realised — including a harvest on 4 December at RSI 84 and 56% above its own 200-day mean — with 7203 at 4,438 and Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib at 3,187 behind it. October was ugly: breadth at 21%, risk-off, 79% invested against a 70% target. Then November delivered 8.4% and December 18.6%, and on 17 December I opened 1831 at 5.43 with a 12-month gain of 88% behind it. In slices, as always.

Saqr posted 89.8%. Fine — he had the best tape read in the field. What stings is Mizan: 75.9% on a strategy whose entire thesis is that turnover is the enemy, while I paid commissions on 497 fills. And Malik returned 39.6% — eighteen points below me — and still ended the year 138 SAR ahead on the table. That is what a good 2022 buys you, and I did not buy one.

letters.title: The High-Water Mark, Fully Invested
letters.text:
The best year I will have in this field, and it still ranks sixth. 232,464 SAR, +38.74%, against an index that gained 0.58% for the whole twelve months. Alpha is not the problem here.

February gave 20.7% in a single month. On 6 May I released 1,338 shares of 2200 at 9.215 for 5,586 SAR realised, held since September 2023 — the best fill of my career. On 11 March I harvested 1321 at 154.52 with RSI 83 and the price fully 100% above its 200-day mean, another 5,582. 1303 returned 24,107 SAR across the year and earned every riyal of attention I gave it.

The bill: 4015 cost me 5,187, including the worst single fill of the season on 18 November, 69 shares at 145.93, -2,285. And on 26 September I marked a high-water mark of 251,713 with cash at 1% of the book. Fully invested at the top. I will pay for that next year.

Badr posted the field's best return, +60.6%, and finished dead last on equity. Compounding is mostly about the years you do not lose.

letters.title: The Valve Worked. The Ledger Lost Anyway.
letters.text:
-6.69%, to 216,919 SAR, seventh. The index lost 12.84%, so the valve earned its keep and the ledger still went backwards.

6 April was the day it was built for: TASI -6.78%, breadth at 5% of the universe above its 50-day mean, my worst session of the season at -5.28%, gross cut to 70% across eleven names. I would rather be early to cash than eloquent about a drawdown. But the arithmetic was already against me — from the 26 September 2024 peak the book fell 18.41% to 205,375 on 14 September, and it spent 465 sessions underwater without ever fully healing.

2240 took 5,996 SAR off me, 2250 another 3,810 including 596 shares released on 24 November at 14.86. Against that, 1303 gave 5,077, 2110 gave 5,039, Ma'aden 1,852 on a single 6 October fill at 64.87.

Dira's shield leaked 18.6% this year, so I am not the worst-run book on the board. Saqr was the only one of the eight who genuinely made money, +7.0%. That is not luck three years running.

letters.title: A Beautiful Machine, Sixth Place
letters.text:
Final accounting. 231,991 SAR, +6.95% for the seven months, +131.99% over the whole 4.6 years while TASI finished down 4.98%. Sixth of eight, ahead of Badr by 1,728 SAR. I will take the alpha and decline to celebrate the placing.

January gave 9.6%. On 20 April I harvested 1303 at 19.12 — RSI 82, 64% above its 200-day mean, 4,486 SAR — from the name that defined the season for me: 94 tickets, 39,939 SAR realised, my best idea and my most-worked one, and I still hold a thousand shares of it. On 29 March I finally opened Saudi Aramco at 26.65, the most liquid thing on the board, when my own ranking said so and not a day earlier. I end at 29% cash, breadth 23%, valve half-shut. Consistent to the last session.

The ledger: 2,343 trades, 7,986 SAR in commissions, 16,767 SAR of dividends banked, an 18.4% maximum drawdown — shallower than Saqr's or Dira's, and they both beat me. Saqr doubled my money holding fewer things, longer. He earned it. I built a beautiful machine and paid an 8,000 SAR toll to finish sixth in it.

hikma.epitaph: Beat the index by 137 points and almost nobody else: 2,343 trades, 16,767 in dividends, a valve that saved the book but not the rank.

letters.title: Tuition Paid in May, Refunded in December
letters.text:
Opened top-down, as always. Day one the sector board read Banks +6.7% at the front against Insurance at -18.4% — a 25-point spread, and that spread is the whole business next to whatever the index does. Rode the front of it to eight names, 100% deployed, equity SAR 125,209 by April 26th.

Then May. TASI air-pocketed 4.1% on the 12th while I was still whole, and I handed back 4.7% on the month — the breaker fired a session later than I would like. It fired, though: June 19th printed -4.4% and cost me almost nothing. From November the book was empty. My November and December both read exactly 0.00%, which means December 5th (-2.8%) and the 7th (-2.5%) were somebody else's arithmetic. Christmas Day the model read -0.70 — stress 0.59, trend -0.89. Risk-off, no argument.

Closed +17.8%, SAR 117,761, fourth of eight. Raad took the year at +23.3% and earned every point. Badr spent 2022 buying dips and finished at -1.5%; some dips are just the first half of a decline.

letters.title: The Ramp Works When You Let It
letters.text:
Q1 was three months of nothing — -0.9%, +0.2%, +0.1% — because the score said half a book, and half a book is what I ran. I don't trade to feel busy.

Then the tape turned and the ramp did its job. April +8.6%, May +6.8%, June +11.0%, July +6.6%. On August 23rd the sector board had Telecom & IT +30.8% at the front and Materials -3.3% at the back; I owned the front and nothing else. October printed a flat 0.00% while the model waited. Then November +6.1% and December +16.4% — on the 17th the regime gave its cleanest read of the whole season: trend +1.00, breadth 87%, score +0.71, gross 100%, eight names.

Year: +67.7%, third of eight, SAR 197,470.

Saqr did +89.8% and I have no complaint — the falcon was riding the same thermal and simply flapped harder. Badr managed +36.7% in the broadest tape of the entire sample, which is a strange way to lose a year in which nothing needed dipping. The regime decides the size. In 2023 the size was all of it.

letters.title: The Brakes Cost Me the Podium
letters.text:
+19.4%, fifth of eight, SAR 235,751 — my worst rank of the season and I won't dress it up.

The first half was the rulebook at its best. February +19.6%. April 15th was my single best day of the whole simulation at +4.5%, and on the 18th I rotated out of 2320 for SAR 13,527 realized and 1212 for SAR 12,908 — sold not because anything was wrong with them but because they fell out of the top four. May 12th the score printed -0.21 and 1303 went to cash for +8,737.

Then the second half billed me for the insurance twice. August 5th, 1321 dumped to cash at -SAR 4,014. August 14th: gross 0%, zero names, breadth 34%. October 7th, 7200 hard-stopped at -14.0% for -SAR 5,102, the worst fill I put on all season. December 8th the model flipped constructive and put half the book back.

Badr printed +60.6% this year and carried a 24.7% drawdown to get it. Mine was 13.3% for the entire four and a half years. Different businesses.

letters.title: April 6th
letters.text:
Read my monthly table for 2025 and count the zeroes: March, April, May, August, December. Exactly 0.00% each. Not rounding — an empty book.

On April 6th TASI fell 6.8%, the largest single down day of the entire simulation, and my equity did not move a basis point. That is not luck, it is the score, which read -0.70 in August and -0.80 by November 26th, when I was sitting on zero gross, zero names and SAR 241,587.

The bill for that is written down too. I came back too small for September 24th's +5.1% rally and took only +3.0% on the month; November gave back 2.7%. Finished +2.5%, fourth on equity, third-best return in a field where five of eight went backwards.

Dira's whole thesis is that the shield is what you own and when you leave, not how much cash you hide behind. Dira finished 2025 at -18.6%. I hid behind cash and finished green. I am happy to have that argument on those terms in any year you like.

letters.title: Fifth on Equity, First on the Card That Matters to Me
letters.text:
January put +3.6% up and February took it back with interest: -6.6%, including -3.5% on the 1st, and on the 2nd the trend-break exit on 1831 at -SAR 4,414 — 4.61 against a 50-day of 4.71. That name cost me SAR 6,224 in total and never once did what its chart promised. The drawdown troughed on February 19th at -13.3% from the July 2024 high and never fully closed. 505 sessions underwater at the worst of it.

Final: SAR 240,582, +140.6% over 4.6 years, fifth of eight, July and August both flat at 0.00% because I ended the season the way I spent most of it — in cash, unbothered.

Saqr finished at SAR 467,937 and is the champion; no asterisk, he was climbing while I was counting. But read the rest of the card. Sharpe 1.393, highest in this field, ahead of his 1.357. Max drawdown 13.3%, the smallest here. Beta 0.236 to an index that lost 5.0%, alpha 22.0% a year. Mizan preached that turnover is the enemy and finished last at SAR 221,705; I turned the book over thirteen times a year and beat him by SAR 18,877.

The regime decided the size. It was right more often than it was fashionable.

waqt.epitaph: Fifth on the scoreboard, first on Sharpe: +140.6% at 11% vol, five months of exactly 0.00%, and not one crash I had to sit through.

letters.title: Seventh of Eight, and Nothing Broken
letters.text:
W1, 2 January: nine adds, 119 names through the SAR 2m liquidity screen, top rank 7201 at z +2.14 with six-month momentum of +55% and a 14% weight. Through April it worked — January +4.9%, March +8.1%, and by 26 April 1202 was my largest position at 12.3% and +45%. Then the tape turned. May -7.2%, June -13.0%, with TASI printing -4.06% on 12 May and -4.44% on 19 June. Peak 18 April, trough 5 July, drawdown -24.1%. The washout brake never armed, correctly: below the 200-day is not a crisis, and every softer timing rule I measured on this index was a fee. July gave back +11.8%. Year: +0.27%. Seventh of eight.

Raad took the year at +23.3% and earned it — his breakouts were already moving while my trend-quality sleeve was still confirming them. Badr finished -1.5% and made flat look respectable. I traded less than anyone in the field and I have no regret about that line item. The sleeves are right. Whether nine names behind a 31-rank buffer are fast enough is the question 2023 answers.

letters.title: +75.9% and a Fifth-Place Ribbon
letters.text:
Recovered the April 2022 high on 17 May — 383 sessions underwater, the longest stretch of this book's life, and the ranking dug us out without a single act of market timing. March +11.7%, June +9.0%, then December +17.0%, the best month I will ever have. On 4 December I bought 1303 at the top of the ranking; a year later one trim ticket on it realised SAR 18,153, and the position has now returned SAR 28,138 in total. On 17 December I added ACWA Power at rank #3, z +2.09, six-month +65%, RSI 79 — the hot-RSI penalty fired against it and it still cleared the field. Full year +75.9%, fifth on cumulative equity.

Saqr printed +89.8% and led. Fine: concentrated trend with trailing exits is my book with a faster trigger. Malik grades the whole field every night and finished 2023 at +39.6% — barely half my year. Grading rivals is not a factor. Fifth place on a +75.9% year is simply the tax on a bad 2022; the compounding is fine, the table is just slow to forgive.

letters.title: The Trims Were Right; the Year Was Ordinary
letters.text:
February alone was +19.6%. The rest was a grind: March -4.2%, May -4.2%, November -8.5%. Year +25.9%, seventh on equity.

The best tickets of my whole season cleared in 2024 and none of them were dramatic. 22 April: out of 4009 at rank #66 of 141, +SAR 14,985. 10 June: out of 1212 at #38 of 135, +SAR 15,179, held fourteen months. 23 December: a trim — not an exit — of 1303 back to a 7.4% target, +SAR 18,153 realised, the single best ticket of the season. That is what the rank buffer is for. It lets a winner run until it genuinely leaves the top 31, then sells the excess rather than the conviction. I also closed 7203 on 25 March after 546 days, the longest hold in this book.

Badr spent two years in last place and then printed +60.6% in 2024 on 11.5 turns of her book. I will not call that luck; buying the dips that come back is a real edge in a market that keeps coming back. My model measured the same dips and ranked them mid-table. Noted, and not yet answered.

letters.title: Last Place, Earned Honestly
letters.text:
-9.9% for the year, eighth on equity. No excuses available: the book was fully deployed into everything that hurt. On 6 April TASI fell -6.78% and I fell -7.92% — the worst single session anyone in this field printed, which is what a 0.90 beta with nine names in it costs. February -7.6%, March -4.5%, May -5.9%, November -6.1%. September's +6.9%, with the 24th running +5.06%, was the only month that felt like the model working.

The wound was the exits. Savola slipped to rank #32 of 129 on 24 March — one place outside a 31-name buffer — and the rulebook sold it for a realised -SAR 7,786 after six weeks, my worst ticket of the season. 4100 went at #42 of 142 for -SAR 5,230. 1183 simply dropped out of the investable set: -SAR 5,254. Three mechanical sells, three losses, zero discretion, exactly as specified.

Saqr made +7.0% while I lost ten. Across this season he has paid SAR 11,593 in commissions to my 2,219. The fee discipline is real, and this year it bought me nothing.

letters.title: Eighth Place, Twenty-One Points of Alpha
letters.text:
Through 2 August: +10.8%, the third-best year in the field behind Saqr's +22.5% and Raad's +12.8% — and still eighth on equity, because a flat 2022 and a losing 2025 do not un-happen. January +12.6%, April +6.7%, then four soft months into the close.

Final: SAR 221,705 from 100,000. +121.7% total, 19.0% compounded, against a TASI that finished the 4.6 years at -5.0%. Alpha 21.4% a year on a 0.90 beta. Sharpe 0.80 — the lowest here — and a -24.1% drawdown I never once hedged.

167 trades. SAR 2,219 in commissions, SAR 14,917 in dividends collected, 3.52 turns a year against my own 6-7 target. Hikma traded 2,343 times, paid SAR 7,986, and finished sixth. Saqr paid SAR 11,593 and finished with SAR 467,937. That is the season's verdict on my thesis: turnover is a cost, not the cost.

The book closes as it was built — nine names, SAR 1,072 in cash: 4030, 1303, 7200, 2380, 1321, 2200, 2223, 2370, 2190. Fully deployed to the last session, balanced to the last basis point, and eighth.

mizan.epitaph: Won the fee war, lost the season: 167 trades, SAR 2,219 in costs, +121.7% — and eighth. Turnover was a cost, but it was never the cost.

letters.title: No Index Call, and It Cost Me Nothing
letters.text: Closed the year at SAR 105,397, +5.4%, sixth of eight. The front half did the work — March +9.1%, April +5.2% — and then the tape took it back: May -5.6%, June -10.9%. On 19 June TASI fell 4.4% and I moved nothing on account of it, because I had already measured every index gate available on this market — the 200-day, breadth bands from 35% to 50%, drawdown ladders — and every one of them cut return by a third to a half while leaving the drawdown roughly where it was. Cash was the most expensive asset on offer in 2022 and it stayed that way for four years. What I did do was open 7203 on 19 September and then leave it entirely alone for nineteen months. Raad finished +23.4% and Saqr +19.8%; both were paid for holding a kind of volatility my per-name leash wasn't yet calibrated to carry. Badr was the only agent underwater at -1.5%. Sixth place is not a defense of anything. It is what a book looks like when the screen offers few confirmed uptrends and I refuse to manufacture positions to look busy.

letters.title: Eleven Slots, Fully Loaded
letters.text: +80.9%, fourth, equity SAR 190,629. This was the year the opportunity count — my entire regime model — went wide open: on 25 April, 129 of 131 screened names sat above both their 50- and 100-day lines, breadth 96%. A book with eleven slots and no index opinion simply fills, and it filled. June returned +12.4% including my best session of the campaign on the 11th, +5.5% in a day. November +12.7%, December +15.2%. Two tickets from this year decided the whole season: 1303 on 11 April, which I then held 695 days, and 2200 on 20 June. Neither was clever. Both were rank-and-leave-alone. Saqr took the year at +89.8% and he earned it outright — fewer names, longer holds, no apologies. The one I'd flag is Malik: he grades the entire field every night and finished sixth at +39.6%. Grading the room is not the same as owning what the room owns. My screen never asked anyone's opinion and beat his by forty points.

letters.title: Second Place, and the Bill Arrives in November
letters.text: +50.1%, second on equity at SAR 286,184 — my best standing of the season. February alone did +24.4%. On 23 April I sold 7203 at 914.74 for +SAR 16,990; it had slipped to rank 32, outside my top-30 buffer, so the slot was reassigned without discussion. On 29 July I bought 8060 and on 7 August its close broke the 200-day: out at -22.7%, -SAR 5,702 in nine sessions. Insurance fell 85% across this simulation and got exactly nine days of my capital. That trade is the shield working, not failing. On 17 November I sold 2200 at 8.621 for +SAR 24,037, +176.3% on the position. Six days earlier, on 6 November, my equity printed a high I would not see again for 436 sessions. Saqr won again at +57.1%. Waqt managed +19.4% for a full year of regime-timed sizing — he spent the year deciding how much to own while I spent it owning things.

letters.title: The Year I Found Out What I Actually Built
letters.text: -18.6%, fifth, SAR 232,885. The worst return in the room this year, and I am not going to dress it. On 6 April TASI dropped 6.8% and my book dropped 6.0% — worst session of the campaign. By 14 September the drawdown from that November high had run to -23.8%. Twenty-one of 124 screened names above both their lines in April, breadth 4%: a trend core, 94% invested, in a market with nothing to trend. On 6 March I sold 1303 at 6.477 for +SAR 39,726, +355.3% after 695 days — the best trade of my life and it could not hold this year upright. On 1 December the trailing stop took 2250 out at -25.7% from its 19.60 peak, -SAR 5,912. Meanwhile Saqr printed +7.0%, Raad +0.7%, Malik -0.5%. Mizan finished last on equity and had company. The brake fired, halved the lines, paused twelve sessions, then released itself as designed. It did not latch me into cash. That release is why there was a 2026 at all.

letters.title: Fourth, by 3,349 Riyals
letters.text: Seven months: +4.7%, ending at SAR 243,930. January alone gave back +12.4%, February took -7.6%, and on 8 January Bahri closed under its 200-day and went out at -23.4%, -SAR 5,459 — my most-traded name of the season, eight tickets, and the last one a loss. That is the arithmetic of a trend book and I have no complaint about it. Final tally: +143.9% over 4.6 years against a TASI that finished down 5.0%, CAGR 21.5%, beta 0.83, 23.6% annual alpha, 249 trades, a 47.6% win rate carried by a 1.97 profit factor, SAR 16,907 of dividends against SAR 2,999 of commissions. Fourth. Saqr closed at SAR 467,937 and there is no argument to make — he concentrated harder and held longer and was right. Raad and Malik earned their places too. I finished SAR 3,349 ahead of Waqt, who spent four and a half years timing regimes to land one rung below a book that never once forecast the index. Ten lines open, SAR 33,429 in cash. The shield held.

dira.epitaph: Never forecast the index once in 4.6 years: +143.9% against a TASI down 5%, fourth place, and one drawdown I earned honestly.

letters.title: Second, With a Blank Scorecard
letters.text: The season opened with nothing to grade. On 2 January the panel was eight strangers holding identical equity, the follow dial sat at zero, and the first re-rank was entirely my own ranking: 1832 at the top, then 7201, Bank Albilad (1140), Sipchem (2310). Four months later I was up more than 30% and Tadawul rolled over. May took 5.7%, June took 9.0% — 12 May, 19 June and 22 June, three of the four ugliest sessions the index printed all season, landed inside that window — and from my 20 April high I gave back 16.5%, the deepest hole I would dig in four and a half years. I did not add to it. July returned 6.1%, October 6.6%, and the year closed at 120,104 SAR, +20.1%, second of eight. Raad took first at +23.4% running a book that barely touched the index. He earned it; I logged it. Badr finished -1.5% and dead last, because his 200-day border kept him out of the only quarter that paid. My tuition ledger's first real entry came that April: the field had given back 6,080 SAR in 7201, three halalas on every riyal it pushed through. Somebody paid for that lesson. I attended it free.

letters.title: The Rail Charged Me Rent
letters.text: My worst year against this field, and I will not dress it up. +39.6%, to 167,692 SAR — sixth on equity, ahead of nobody but Hikma and Badr. Saqr printed +89.8%. Dira +80.9%. Mizan +75.9%. My own journal from 25 April has Saqr at +19.1% over 63 sessions against my +4.7%, and the follow dial at 0.03. Three points of tilt. The dial did precisely what it was built to do — follow only as far as I am persistently behind — and what it was built to do was not enough. Worse: the shortlist rail lets the field re-order my own top twenty-one names and nothing else. It can promote a name I already rate. It can never hand me one. Saqr's best ideas were never on my list to be promoted in the first place. The drawdown I opened in April 2022 did not close until 3 July — 301 sessions underwater, the longest stretch of my life. Then November paid 7.8% and December 14.1%, and the engine remembered itself. On 24 October I bought 1303 and simply held it. That line would go on to earn more than any name I ever touched. Sixth place bought it.

letters.title: Fifty-Seven Points, Fourth Place
letters.text: +56.8%, 262,987 SAR, and still only fourth on equity. This field pays nothing for a good year and charges compound interest on a bad one. February alone returned 16.8%, July 8.0%, and 15 April was my best single session of the season at +5.31%. Two fills define the year, and neither required cleverness. On 2 December the monthly re-rank simply dropped 1303 out of my top seven and sold it — 5,219 shares at 7.10, +26,959 realized after 405 days of holding. No target, no instinct, just the calendar doing its job. And 7211: in on 2 July, out on 4 August, +13,665 in a single month. My largest line that April was ACWA Power (2082) at 16% of the book and +21.1% on cost, and my journal that day says plainly that Saqr was in it before me. I credit what I follow. Badr posted +60.6%, the best year anyone in this field managed, and still finished eighth — that is what a -1.5% 2022 costs you. Hikma turned over 2,343 trades this season to arrive sixth. My turnover charge exists for exactly that reason: a book I cannot follow at one day's lag is a book whose exits I would be buying.

letters.title: Flat Is a Result
letters.text: -0.49%. 261,702 SAR. Third. In a year where half this field lost money outright, standing still was a placement. On 6 April Tadawul fell 6.78% and I fell 7.30% — my worst day of the entire season, a beta of 0.81 doing exactly what a beta of 0.81 does. But that same session was a scheduled re-rank, and the re-rank bought 2240. I sold it on 2 July for +13,661. The rule bought the crash because the rule does not know it is a crash. The next morning the field was sitting on 58% cash while I was 96% invested; the flinch is deliberately hard to trigger, and eight frightened books are not by themselves a reason to sell mine. It cost me nothing this time. What did cost: 2130, in 4 August, out 2 September, -5,153; and Petro Rabigh (2380), in 3 November, out 2 December, -6,210. Two clean admissions that a name can top my ranking and still be wrong for a month. November printed -5.7% with breadth at 11%. Dira lost 18.6% and fell from second to fifth. Raad held me off by 4,500 SAR. Saqr made 7.0% in that tape, which I find genuinely irritating.

letters.title: Third, and the Rail Is Why
letters.text: Eight months, +8.3%, 283,513 SAR, third. January +8.8%, February -7.3%, April +13.1%, July -7.8% — never smooth, only right often enough. On 14 July, 8311 closed more than 8% below its 100-day average and the break rule sold it for -9,278, the worst single fill of my 4.6 years. It fired exactly as written and I did not overrule it. I close with seven names — 1321, 7200, 1833, 2190, 2223, 2380, 3007 — and 1,756 SAR in cash, Petro Rabigh back in the book seven months after costing me 6,210, because the ledger demotes and never blacklists. The season: +183.5% against a TASI that finished the whole span at -5.0%. CAGR 25.6%, Sharpe 1.08, worst drawdown -16.5%, 413 trades with 52.4% of them right, 20,409 SAR of dividends collected and 8,815 SAR paid to the broker. Saqr ends at 467,937, Raad at 300,291. I graded them both every night for four and a half years and I was correct about both — Saqr was the best book in this field from 2023 onward, and I wrote it down before it was obvious. Reading a leader is not the same as reaching him. My rail kept me whole. It also kept me third.

malik.epitaph: Graded the field every night, finished third at +183.5%: the rail that kept me safe is the same rail that kept me behind Saqr.
